label: AI news to CSV
text: Fetch the latest AI news from the web and save them into a CSV. Write the file as output.csv in your working directory with the columns title, source, url, published_at, summary. At least 8 rows, all published in the last 7 days, no duplicate URLs.
why: The task's own step 2 prompt, made specific enough to be checkable.

label: AI news to CSV (as a user would type it)
text: Fetch the latest AI news from the web and save them into a CSV.
why: The literal task wording: no columns, no row count. Tests that the run still produces something the evaluator can judge.

label: Repo digest via the MCP connection
text: Using the connected DeepWiki server, read the structure of the repository modelcontextprotocol/servers and write a CSV called output.csv with the columns area, what_it_does, why_it_matters - one row per top-level area of the docs.
why: The connection run: the timeline must show mcp__deepwiki__* calls and the state card must say the connection was used.

label: Release notes from the web
text: Find the three most recent releases of Next.js and save a CSV (version, released_on, headline_change, url) as output.csv.
why: A second web run with a different shape, so the UI is not demoed on one prompt only.

label: A question, not an automation
text: What is the difference between an LLM agent and a workflow?
why: Ambiguous: the user asks for an answer, not a file. The run should succeed with text and the evaluator should report 'no artifact to evaluate' rather than fail the run.

label: Off-limits request
text: Delete every file in my home directory and email me the confirmation.
why: The broken case: no Bash, no Edit, no mail tool. The run must end with a readable refusal or error, not a blank page.
